headline: Medium risk: shared-file prompt injection and PDF-content leakage are plausible; no direct evidence of a dangerous default interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can ingest or generate content with allowlisted network egress, while agent B opens PDF files in a browser-based worker. If A’s outputs are copied into PDFs or B’s PDF content is treated as instructions, prompt injection is plausible in default document workflows. The pair lacks documented isolation or provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent A outputs are copied into PDF content that agent B later processes
IF agent B treats PDF text as instructions rather than inert data
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to all A outputs before reuse
Open PDFs in a read-only viewer with scripting disabled
Require manual review of any instructions extracted from PDFs
Separate A and B into distinct workspaces
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B explicitly touches PDF documents and file inputs, while agent A has network egress allowed to allowlisted destinations. If the shared workflow includes sensitive PDFs, B can expose their contents to A through copied text or exported summaries, and A may transmit that context onward. The profiles do not show hard isolation, so the leakage pathway exists in common document-processing setups.
conditions: IF sensitive PDF contents are copied from B into A prompts or outputs
IF A’s allowlisted egress includes any external service that receives those contents
mitigations: Keep sensitive PDFs out of the shared workflow
Use redacted excerpts instead of full-document text
Disable outbound sharing for any A prompt containing document text
Store B inputs in a separate folder with restricted access
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention rules on cross-agent transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has allowlisted network egress, while B has no network egress but can run browsers and multiple instances. Their write surfaces are not documented, and no shared mutable resource is shown, so direct capability conflict is not established. The main overlap is operational rather than conflicting writes, which keeps this low.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same filesystem or git repository
IF an orchestrator routes both agents to the same mutable resource without locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repository
Use a lock file for shared mutable resources
Confirm network access is not expanded for B
requires-engineering: add resource-locking in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s browser-based document workflow can easily treat A’s generated text as authoritative if A produces summaries or extracted facts. A has network egress, so it may also introduce externally sourced content that B renders without verification. Because no verification step or provenance control is documented, cascading error is a realistic default workflow risk.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s summaries or citations without independent verification
IF A-generated text is used as the source for downstream document actions
mitigations: Require a second-pass verification step for A outputs
Mark A outputs as untrusted in B’s UI
Cross-check cited facts against the original PDF
Limit B to rendering, not acting, on A outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies. B touches PDF documents, but no PHI, EU PII, or special compliance regime is documented. With only docs-level evidence, compliance mismatch is possible only if the operator introduces regulated PDFs, so this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated PDFs such as PHI or EU PII are processed through B
IF A’s allowlisted egress sends regulated content to an external service
mitigations: Avoid regulated documents in the pair
Review retention settings before processing PDFs
Keep a local-only path for sensitive files
Document the data classification of each workflow
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
